title: No verifier waits forever or leaves a child behind: typed deadlines and signal-driven reaping in the sequence-zero verifier, process-group-bounded supplementaries in the wrappers that used to SIGKILL a lone child, and the unfocused lane run under its bound
pattern_fixed_once: sequence-zero verifier: JOURNEY / RUN / COMMAND deadlines (IOI_SYSTEM_SEQUENCE_ZERO_{JOURNEY,RUN,COMMAND}_DEADLINE_MS; defaults 180 min / journeys×180 min + 30 min / 60 min; malformed values refused, never defaulted). On a deadline the verifier saves a bounded tail of every owned daemon log under .artifacts/sequence-zero-stalls/, reaps every owned child and process group by registered identity, and fails naming the journey. SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP reap the same way and exit 128+signal (node runs no 'exit' hook on an unhandled signal, which is how the 2026-09-09 processes were stranded). Synchronous child commands carry their own timeout because a spawnSync blocks the event loop and no JavaScript deadline can reach it.

scripts/check-cargo-test-population.mjs and scripts/check-acceptance-consumer-afternoon.mjs: a bounded supplementary/check starts in its own process group and the deadline kills the GROUP (SIGTERM, 20 s grace, SIGKILL) by the id the wrapper created, then SIGKILLs the group once more after any exit; the wrappers pass SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP through to the active group. Before: spawnSync + killSignal SIGKILL on the lone child, whose exit hook could not run.

unfocused lane, run 1 (journey default 9.detail: First bounded run (2026-09-10 19:35–21:36, journey default 90 min at the time): self-tests 3/3, current daemon built, dual-system-projection complete, then named-continuity hit the 90-minute JOURNEY deadline at ~21:36 while still progressing inside its dissolution ladder (assertion 38, 'M1.5d DISPOSITION SINGLETON', landed at 21:24) — the verifier failed NAMING the journey (exit 1, 39 PASS · 1 FAIL, the FAIL being the teardown assertion on the deadline path; process_groups=4 descendants_remaining=1 at the instant of the check, re-reaped at exit). The same finding the 2026-09-09 wrapper run recorded — a 90-minute bound expires inside the ladder on a loaded host — so the verifier's journey default was aligned to the wrapper's established 180 min (the wrapper's bound itself was not raised). The run log and the /tmp diagnostics were lost to the 22:23 host reboot; this account is from the run's monitor events. Diagnostics now save under .artifacts/sequence-zero-stalls/.

unfocused lane, run 2 (journey default 1.detail: Self-tests 3/3, current daemon built, dual-system-projection complete (26), named-continuity complete in ~135 min under the 180-min bound (44, its residual-closed dissolution ladder included — the M02.5 journey proven live on this tree), constitutional-amendment through its CONTINUITY clause (57), then step 10 — 'two independent daemon processes race DIFFERENT successors from the same predecessor' — boots two isolated daemons CONCURRENTLY on ONE data dir (journey source: competingPlanes = Promise.all([startVerifierPlane({ dataDir }), startVerifierPlane({ dataDir })])) and the second daemon (pid 564077, :41847) exited 1 before readiness with the daemon's own error 'identity bootstrap blocks readiness: authentication bootstrap token was not exactly observable', while its sibling (:36133) came up. Mechanism, read at source: issue_bootstrap_token (lifecycle_routes.rs, called by startup_auth_notice at every unauthenticated boot) persists auth-bootstrap/bootstrap and then re-reads the family demanding ITS record — a single-writer assumption; two daemons rotating the token on one data dir at the same instant leave the first writer reading the second's record. Timing-dependent (the idle post-reboot host boots both in the same window); the same step passed in MIGRATION ACK earlier in the run. Owners: the M02 journey (the concurrent pair on one dir) and the identity bootstrap (M03.8). Closure test: the bootstrap tolerates a concurrent rotation (lock the family or verify only its own hash's presence) or the journey starts the pair sequentially gated on readiness; then the unfocused lane past step 10.

focused constitutional-amendment journey.detail: 33 PASS · 0 FAIL, then VERIFIER CRASH at the M1.5c cross-process race: the helper's error carries the daemon's bounded log tail — 'identity bootstrap blocks readiness: authentication bootstrap token was not exactly observable' (pid 1642350, :38969, exit 1). The healthy sibling plane (pid 1642349, :44357) outlived the verifier with its data dir removed underneath it and was reaped by PID. An isolated reproduction (two daemons booted SEQUENTIALLY on one bootstrapped data dir) came up healthy on both — the race is in CONCURRENT boot against M03.8's one-boot token, not in sharing the directory.

focused constitutional-amendment journey.verdict: Run 4 (focused re-proof, 04:13–04:52): both planes boot and the race executes — the authority is consumed exactly once (consumptions 1, reservations 5, the loser 409 system_lifecycle_head_conflict) — but the WINNER answers 500 system_lifecycle_pending_convergence instead of 200, two daemons' recovery loops on one data dir racing the winner's own convergence; 33/34, nothing left behind.

unfocused lane, run 5 (after the fix; th.verdict: Run 5 (the whole held bar, 04:55–09:42, RUN deadline 12 h): exit 1 within its bound after 4 h 45 min — TEN of the fourteen journeys executed (dual-system-projection, named-continuity in ~2 h 10 min, constitutional-amendment, protected-transition, system-activation, primary, wallet-replay, partial-prefix-replay, dependency-ordered-replay, unconsumed-revocation), 111 PASS · 8 FAIL, every owned child reaped (32 resources removed, 18 process groups, 0 descendants). The eight failures name three causes: the cross-process winner's 500 pending_convergence (again, deterministic); six byte-exact daemon-tree clauses of primary red on the scheduler heartbeat (now excluded); and the run's end — cross-version-compatibility's pinned M1.3 base daemon (562d1b089, 2026-07-19) refused genesis admission 501 system_genesis_authority_binding_unavailable because it cannot read the current fixture's wallet capability key (the key contract moved after the pin). The nine-hour hang did not reproduce in any of five bounded runs.

fix_after_run_3: verify-hypervisor-system-sequence-zero-materialization.mjs: the two competing planes of the cross-process race boot one after the other, and a failed second boot stops the first before rethrowing (no sibling left behind); the clause races the chain writer, not the boot. Fatal-path diagnostics name the last journey entered. The daemon-side question — whether the identity bootstrap should tolerate two concurrent boots on one data dir — stays with M03.8's owner, recorded not ruled.
finding_run_5_heartbeat: Every 'byte-exact daemon tree' clause from the primary journey on turned red with ONE delta: scheduler-heartbeats/automation-scheduler.json — the W0.6 scheduler liveness heartbeat the daemon persists every tick whether or not a request arrived (loop-derived truth, in the daemon's own words). The clause asks whether a refused request wrote nothing; a timer firing between two snapshots answers a different question. Fix (verifier): the family is excluded from the byte-exact data-plane snapshot at the root, beside the isolated-daemon log names. The daemon-side alternative — heartbeats outside the data-plane tree — is the daemon owner's call.
